summary: Feed s183_triple to IDS is degraded: 21.3% duplicate packets, 45.9% one-way TCP sessions, and 63.4% encrypted bytes exceeding 60% tolerance. IDS requires bidirectional, deduplicated, inspectable traffic for stateful detection.

findings.root_cause: 21.3% duplicates (349/1637) indicates overlapping SPAN/mirror sessions or multiple TAPs feeding the same broker without deduplication, causing the same packet to be delivered twice.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles processing duplicates, inflates event counts, skews analytics and can cause missed detections due to state confusion and resource waste.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop duplicate copies before IDS, restoring accurate traffic counts and freeing IDS resources for real detection.

findings.root_cause: 45.9% of TCP sessions (50/109) are one-way, typical of asymmetric routing where only one direction is tapped/SPANned or broker is forwarding directions to different tools without aggregating both sides of a flow to this IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and stateful signatures; one-way traffic prevents stream reconstruction, causing missed exploits, broken flow tracking, and high false-negative rate.

recommended_fix.why: Configure broker to aggregate both directions of each flow (5-tuple hashing) to the same IDS port so it sees complete bidirectional sessions.

findings.root_cause: 63.4% of bytes are encrypted vs 60% IDS tolerance, meaning majority of payload is TLS/encrypted and opaque to IDS without decryption.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true but cannot inspect encrypted payload, reducing detection coverage for payload-based signatures and allowing threats inside TLS to bypass detection.

recommended_fix.why: Add SSL visibility appliance or broker decryption capability to provide cleartext to IDS or enrich with metadata, bringing encrypted share within IDS tolerance.
